title: Latency Envelope Negotiator & Tenant Priority Resolver for Continuous Batching
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description:
Problem:
- We see intermittent tail latency regressions on multi-tenant GPUs during mixed short+long request workloads. Root causes cross batching admission, KV cache pressure, and sudden memory spikes when several tenants allocate transient KV working sets. Current mechanisms (static tenant weights + hard eviction) either over-throttle bursty tenants or let background spike workloads degrade p95 for latency-sensitive customers.

Goal:
- Implement a SLO-aware 'envelope negotiator' that dynamically assigns per-tenant latency envelopes and uses those envelopes to arbitrate admission, soft-interrupts, and cache residency. The system should balance fairness and SLOs while minimizing token cost and GPU memory churn.

Design overview:
1) Latency Envelopes:
   - Each tenant has an assigned envelope: target_p50_ms and target_p95_ms over a sliding window (default 1m/5m). Envelopes are derived from plan tier and observed SLAs.
   - The envelope defines a maximum allowed batching delay and a burst token budget (credits) that can be consumed to temporarily exceed steady-state throughput.

2) Negotiator Service (lightweight in-serving control):
   - Runs on the serving node control plane. Continuously monitors per-tenant metrics: observed latency distribution, KV hit ratio, KV working set size, GPU alloc, and active batch occupancy.
   - Computes a per-tenant pressure score: f(latency_deviation, kv_eviction_rate, gpu_mem_delta, recent_interrupt_count). Pressure score feeds into admission decisions and cache retention priority.

3) Admission & Degradation Actions:
   - Soft admission steering: when pressure high, new requests are offered either: (a) immediate admission with degraded model variant (quantized or shorter sequence cap), (b) delayed admission into a limited fast-path batch, or (c) redirected to a lower-cost region/pool if configured.
   - Soft-interrupt semantics: instead of hard preemption that drops KV, we implement interrupt-with-resume where the request is paused at safe boundaries and requeued with higher priority based on envelope urgency. This reduces KV thrash compared to evict-on-preempt.

4) KV Residency & Prioritization:
   - Assign KV retention priority proportional to envelope SLA tightness and recent hit-rates. Low-priority tenants are allowed to have their KV pages demoted to host-memory spill or serialized checkpointing if the node supports it.
   - Implement a compact-and-coalesce pass that runs opportunistically between large batches to defragment GPU memory and reduce transient peak allocations.

5) Tenant Burst Credits and Refill:
   - Each tenant has a burst-credit bucket sized by commit level and historical usage. Credits replenish at a controlled rate. Using credits allows temporary envelope stretching without immediate degradation of other tenants.

6) Metrics & Signals:
   - Primary: tenant_p95_latency_ms, tenant_p50_latency_ms, batch_wait_ms, kv_hit_ratio, kv_eviction_rate, gpu_memory_used_mb, interruptions_per_min, resumed_requests_ratio.
   - Objectives: keep p95 within envelope 95% of the time; keep eviction rate < X%; limit resume churn to < 5% of requests.

7) Config API / Console knobs:
   - Per-tenant: envelope targets, credit bucket size, allowed degradation variants, redirect targets.
   - Node-level: memory compaction frequency, soft-interrupt thresholds, maximum resume queue length.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): implement negotiator in simulation mode on a subset of hosts (decision logs only). Train thresholds using historical traces (SLO-aware replay).
- Phase 2 (pilot): enable soft-interrupt + envelope enforcement for non-critical tenants; monitor impact on tail and KV churn.
- Phase 3 (wider rollout): enable for all tenants with conservative defaults; expose tenant console controls.

Testing & Benchmarks:
- Replay historical 72-hour production trace with workload mixes (50/30/20 short/medium/long) and measure p95 lift, KV eviction delta, memory compaction overhead, and token cost change. Target: p95 improvement >= 15% for lat-sensitive tenants and eviction reduction >= 25% with < 3% CPU overhead for control plane.

Trade-offs & Risks:
- Complexity: soft-interrupt + resume requires careful checkpointing at safe tokens boundaries. We'll limit resume points initially to generator tokens boundaries to reduce implementation complexity.
- Memory compaction may add jitter; keep it opportunistic and throttled.
- Burst credits may be gamed by noisy tenants; implement rate limiting and cross-tenant fairness checks.

Open decisions:
- Default envelope sizing heuristics for new tenants (static vs adaptive ramp).
- Full host-spill vs partial page compress strategies for demoted KV.
- How to surface resumed-request artifacts in tracing for debugging.

Acceptance criteria:
- Automated canary pass shows no more than 1% regression for p50 for high-tier tenants; clear p95 improvement for targeted tenants in pilot; no increase in out-of-memory incidents in pilot hosts.
